title: Asymptotic Metrological Scaling and Concentration in Chaotic Floquet Dynamics
abstract: We study quantum sensing with Floquet chaotic dynamics generated by Haar random unitary gates. The metrological resources consist of three ingredients: A given initial state, a set number of Haar random unitary gates and the sensing gates. There are two natural ways of organizing the resources: the first one is the "control" protocol, where the random unitary gates act as random controls and intertwine with the deterministic sensing gates and the second one is the "state-preparation" protocol, where random unitary gates play the role of preparing the metrological useful states. In each protocol, we consider both global Haar random unitary gates and a set of local two-site Haar random unitary gates that forms a Floquet random quantum circuit (RQC) respectively. We find linear, shot-noise scaling of the metrological precision, quantified by the quantum Fisher information (QFI), in the asymptotic limit when the Hilbert space dimension becomes large, and quantum advantages beyond linear scaling in the non-asymptotic regimes. We also bound the fluctuation of the QFI using concentration inequalities. Our analytical findings are corroborated by numerical simulations. Finally, along the way of analyzing the precision limit, we prove an empirical conjecture of RQC: In the asymptotic limit of large local Hilbert space dimension, the Floquet operator of a Floquet RQC essentially behaves like a global unitary operator.

evidence.abstract: We study quantum sensing with Floquet chaotic dynamics generated by Haar random unitary gates. The metrological resources consist of three ingredients: A given initial state, a set number of Haar random unitary gates and the sensing gates. There are two natural ways of organizing the resources: the first one is the "control" protocol, where the random unitary gates act as random controls and intertwine with the deterministic sensing gates and the second one is the "state-preparation" protocol, where random unitary gates play the role of preparing the metrological useful states. In each protocol, we consider both global Haar random unitary gates and a set of local two-site Haar random unitary gates that forms a Floquet random quantum circuit (RQC) respectively. We find linear, shot-noise scaling of the metrological precision, quantified by the quantum Fisher information (QFI), in the asymptotic limit when the Hilbert space dimension becomes large, and quantum advantages beyond linear scaling in the non-asymptotic regimes. We also bound the fluctuation of the QFI using concentration inequalities. Our analytical findings are corroborated by numerical simulations. Finally, along the way of analyzing the precision limit, we prove an empirical conjecture of RQC: In the asymptotic limit of large local Hilbert space dimension, the Floquet operator of a Floquet RQC essentially behaves like a global unitary operator.

title: Meta-Offline and Distributional Multi-Agent RL for Risk-Aware Decision-Making
abstract: Mission critical applications, such as UAV-assisted IoT networks require risk-aware decision-making under dynamic topologies and uncertain channels. We propose meta-conservative quantile regression (M-CQR), a meta-offline distributional MARL algorithm that integrates conservative Q-learning (CQL) for safe offline learning, quantile regression DQN (QR-DQN) for risk-sensitive value estimation, and model-agnostic meta-learning (MAML) for rapid adaptation. Two variants are developed: meta-independent CQR (M-I-CQR) and meta-CTDE-CQR. In a UAV-based communication scenario, M-CTDE-CQR achieves up to 50% faster convergence and outperforms baseline MARL methods, offering improved scalability, robustness, and adaptability for risk-sensitive decision-making. Code is available at https://github.com/Eslam211/MA_Meta_ODRL

title: Experimental Results of EDRL in the DMControl-GB Environment
abstract: This dataset is the DMControl-GB (DeepMind Control Generalization Benchmark) visual reinforcement learning generalization ability evaluation result dataset, mainly aimed at providing data support for quantifying and comparing the robustness of different reinforcement learning algorithms in the face of significant visual differences. In the data generation and acquisition stage, this dataset relies on the continuous physical control benchmark suite developed by DeepMind, and is obtained by running automated testing scripts in a set simulation environment. All participating models completed 500000 exploration and training steps uniformly in the original benchmark environment without visual interference, and were then deployed to a testing environment lacking reward signals and prior knowledge for performance evaluation. To reduce the interference of occasional factors, all tests were independently run under 5 different random seeds and the final results were statistically analyzed. This dataset comprehensively records the experimental results of the EDRL algorithm and its comparison with seven mainstream baseline methods (SAC, DrQ, RAD, SODA, SVEA, SGQN, MaDi). Taking the core performance comparison table as an example, the records in the data table cover the performance of different algorithms under two levels of environmental error: one is the video_ easy mode that replaces dynamic backgrounds but retains ground shadows, and the other is the video_ hard mode that removes ground and shadow references and has severe distribution offset. The row labels of the data table represent specific combinations of algorithms and testing tasks, while the column labels detail key quantitative indicators such as environment name, interference mode, average round reward (Mean), and standard deviation (Std). The core unit of measurement involved is the "single round comprehensive return score", and the effective value range is strictly standardized between 0 and 1000. In addition, the dataset also includes a detailed table of ablation experiment records for the internal mechanism of the EDRL algorithm, including independent feature decoupling, reconstruction, state transition loss function, and multidimensional performance data when replacing the CNN/CNN-LSTM backbone network. In terms of error control in data, the inherent statistical error of data mainly comes from the randomness in the exploration process of reinforcement learning and the inherent variance of neural network initialization. To address this reasonable error, this dataset has been normalized by displaying the mean and standard deviation.

Gurobi remains opt-in.- `docs/developer.md`: architecture, solver-implementation guide, CLI reference, deferred-items list.- Dolan-Moré performance profile (`scripts/27_dolan_more.py`, `results/dolan_more_*.csv`, §VI-G of the paper). ### Changed- Penalty / Holm-Bonferroni family expanded from 10 pairs to 11 pairs (added BALS-warm QAOA vs. BALS).- Proposition 2 "Conditional scale invariance" replaces the earlier unconditional statement; ε-floor regime boundary is now explicit.- Paper-visible artifact tag bumped from `srp-hubo:v1.0` to `srp-hubo:v2.0`; new Zenodo DOI minted for v2.0 (see `CITATION.cff`). ### Fixed- `jsonschema` draft-version compatibility: schemas now declare Draft-07 so the bundled validator works under `jsonschema>=3.2`. ## [1.0.0] - 2026-04-19 (TQE submission) ### Added- Four synthetic benchmark regimes (gaussian / heavy / skewed / stress) generated by a single-factor model with configurable skew and excess kurtosis, in `src/instances.py::build_synthetic_panel`.- `scripts/19_bootstrap_variance.py`: 10k-resample bootstrap CIs on median gap + BALS-warm non-monotonic-p diagnosis.- `scripts/20_q_grid.py`: full $5\times5$ $(q_2, q_3)$ stress grid.- `scripts/21_mps_scaling_deep.py`: MPS scaling to $p \le 3$, $\chi \le 128$, $n \le 24$.- `scripts/22_budget_parity.py`: compute-budget Pareto sweep for BALS/SA/GA/bSB/QAOA.- `scripts/23_run_synthetic_benchmark.py`: runs the full solver ladder on the four synthetic regimes.- `scripts/24_tqe_statistics.py`: Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with Holm-Bonferroni adjustment; rank-biserial effect sizes; Wilson-score exact-hit CIs.- `scripts/25_tqe_artifacts.py`: TQE-specific figures and LaTeX macros.- Per-solver `n_evals` instrumentation in BALS/SA/GA/bSB so matched- evaluation-count comparisons are possible.- Dockerfile, pinned `requirements.txt`, CITATION.cff, LICENSE, this CHANGELOG. ### Changed- `paper/main_tqe.tex`: new journal-length paper targeting IEEE Transactions on Quantum Engineering. ## [0.9.0] - 2026-04-15 (QCE26 RESP revision) Initial revision for the IEEE Quantum Week conference track. See`paper/main_resp.tex` for the submitted version.

title: Privacy-Preserving and Verifiable Federated Learning Framework for Biometric Authentication at the Edge
abstract: Federated learning (FL) has emerged as a pivotal privacy-preserving paradigm for training models across decentralized biometric datasets. However, integrating secure biometric verification and data integrity in FL remains challenging, especially under non-IID distributions and resource constraints in edge environments. This paper introduces BPVFL, a novel Biometric Privacy-preserving and Verifiable Federated Learning framework, which synergizes differential privacy, cryptographic signatures, and photoplethysmogram (PPG)-based biometric recognition. Distinct from prior works, BPVFL supports both verifiable model updates and privacy-preserving identity authentication through a dual-layer protection scheme. We propose a customized privacy noise mechanism tailored for biometric features and a lightweight signature protocol to trace and validate local contributions. Experimental evaluations on three biometric datasets (SigD, BIDMC, TBME) demonstrate that BPVFL achieves over 92.7% accuracy under strong privacy guarantees, while reducing communication costs via deep network modularization. To substantiate verifiability beyond provenance, we further integrate an optional Correctness Verification Layer (CVL) based on remote attestation, which makes accepted updates protocol-correctness verifiable (i.e., generated by an approved clipping/noising/training pipeline) at a small constant overhead. We provide an empirical comparison to representative verifiable FL designs along the axes of client cryptographic time, extra uplink, and end-to-end round latency, clarifying the engineering trade-offs for edge biometric services.

title: Prototype Learning-Based Few-Shot Medical Image Segmentation Framework Using Clip-Aided U-Net Model
abstract: Medical image segmentation is crucial for automated clinical diagnostics, but is often hindered by the scarcity of annotated data. To address this, we propose a novel few-shot learning-based segmentation framework that integrates the complementary strengths of U-Net, for precise boundary localization, and CLIP, for rich semantic generalization. Our method introduces a cross-attention fusion mechanism to align support prototypes, image embeddings, and task-specific textual prompts, thereby enabling robust segmentation from limited examples. Extensive experiments on PanNuke, GlaS and Kvasir-SEG datasets demonstrate that our model achieves state-of-the-art performance across 3-shot, 5-shot, and 10-shot settings. The source code of the proposed model and additional results are available at: https://github.com/SaptarshiPani/CLIP-based-U-Net/.

title: Multi Stage Training with Dynamic Data Balancing for Multilingual Speech Recognition and Translation
abstract: Training large-scale multilingual speech models is often hindered by severe data imbalances across tasks, languages, and corpora. We introduce a systematic, multi-stage training framework to ad-dress this challenge. First, for pre-training on 1.7 million hours of speech across 25 languages, we propose an inverted two-tier sampling policy that prioritizes balancing corpora within each language before balancing across languages, enhancing data diversity. Second, during fine-tuning, we apply a dynamic data balancing schedule that smoothly transitions the data mixture from the initial imbalanced state to a targeted, high-quality distribution using a co-sine schedule. This gradual adaptation prevents catastrophic forget-ting and maximizes performance. Our resulting 1-billion parameter model, Canary-1B-v2, demonstrates the success of this methodology, achieving state-of-the-art multilingual ASR results and speech translation performance competitive with models twice its size, all while maintaining high inference efficiency.

title: T-CAMEL: Teammate-Causal-Aware Multi-Agent Learning
abstract: In multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL), modeling teammates is crucial for effective cooperation. However, most existing methods rely on statistical correlations, lacking causal modeling, which can result in poor interpretability and generalization. To address these problems, this paper proposes a novel MARL framework, T-CAMEL (Teammate-Causal-Aware Multi-Agent Learning). The framework models the effect of teammate behavior via causal graph, with causal discovery learning the structure. By treating the resulting causal graph as a latent variable, T-CAMEL formulates its objective as a variational inference problem, using maximum likelihood estimation to capture causal relationships in teammate interactions and enhance strategy optimization. Furthermore, the framework is algorithm-agnostic and compatible with various causal algorithms. Experiments on discrete and continuous tasks show T-CAMEL facilitates performance improvements across common reinforcement learning methods, and remains robust to causal graph imperfections such as bias, noise, and confounders.

title: Resolving Low-Rank Update Limitations for Memory-Efficient Visual Neural Network Training
abstract: Training large visual neural networks is highly memory-intensive, with optimizer states often acting as the main bottleneck. While memory-efficient subspace optimizers (MeSO) alleviate this by projecting gradients into low-dimensional subspaces, they severely limit updates to restricted subspaces—this degrades optimization expressivity and traps pretraining in suboptimal regions, a critical issue for visual tasks requiring broad parameter exploration. To address this long-standing limitation, we propose ViLaX(Visual Low-rank to High-rank Update eXtension), a novel dual-factor reparameterization framework that achieves low-rank gradient compression while decoupling the optimizer update rank. By factorizing each weight matrix into two low-rank components and applying independent MeSO updates to each, ViLaX enables high-rank effective updates to the original weights, a key innovation that preserves memory efficiency without sacrificing optimization capability. Extensive experiments on CIFAR-10/100 and Tiny ImageNet demonstrate ViLaX’s superiority: it outperforms state-of-the-art low-rank MeSO methods in pretraining accuracy, solving the critical memory-expressivity tradeoff that has challenged visual neural network training.

title: Knowledge Distillation via Generative Reconstruction Pathways for End-to-End Automatic Speech Recognition
abstract: End-to-end automatic speech recognition (ASR) has achieved remarkable progress, with encoder-only models based on the connectionist temporal classification (CTC) objective being widely adopted for their efficiency and simplicity. However, the large model size of state-of-the-art systems remains a major obstacle for deployment in resource-constrained scenarios. Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a promising solution to compress ASR models while preserving accuracy, but most existing approaches rely on point-wise feature alignment losses, which bias the student toward reproducing local correspondences of teacher features. In this work, we propose a generative reconstruction pathway knowledge distillation (GRP-KD) framework that leverages flow matching and diffusion processes to achieve richer knowledge transfer. By treating teacher features as empirical distributions, GRP-KD formulates distillation as a generative reconstruction task that drives the student to approximate the distributional structure of teacher representations. Experiments on the LibriSpeech and GigaSpeech datasets demonstrate that GRP-KD consistently outperforms feature alignment–based KD while retaining a compact parameter footprint.

title: CDT: Robust Detection of DoH Tunnels Via Background Association
abstract: DNS over HTTPS (DoH) enhances user privacy by encrypting queries and is rapidly supplanting legacy DNS. Yet this capability also affords adversaries a covert channel for malicious communications. Although existing detection methods report high accuracy on public datasets, their robustness to adaptive or obfuscation-aware attacks remains uncertain. We show that public DoH datasets exhibit systematic distributional differences between benign and malicious flows (e.g., packet sizes and timing), which can inflate reported accuracy. To stress-test detectors, we develop a browser-based, highly obfuscated DoH tunnel that inherits native packetization and padding and supports C2/exfiltration; on this traffic, state-of-the-art detectors drop from 99% to 72% F1-score. We then introduce CDT—integrating per-flow statistical features, DNS segment-level descriptors, and background-traffic association analysis—to exploit behavioral context. Across public and in-house datasets, CDT achieves F1-score up to 99%, demonstrating strong generalization and robustness.

title: Train2explain: Training Optimization for Explanation Improvement
abstract: Despite the great effort that is being devoted to the investigation of explainability methods to improve Fairness, Universality, Traceability, Usability, Robustness and Explainability of deep networks, the picture is still unfocused calling for novel solutions addressing one or more of such properties. In this work, we propose a closed-loop solution injecting explainability criteria in the training process, so to reach the twofold goal of controlling overfitting and improving gradient-based explanations’ reliability. To this end, we propose a novel training objective that guides the network toward more stable gradients by introducing the Misalignment Attribution metric. Experiments on synthetic datasets show that our approach produces smoother gradient fields while preserving accuracy, as well as explanations that are more robust and reliable due to the reduced dependency on outliers. These results highlight the importance of incorporating interpretability criteria into the training process.

To this end, we propose a novel training objective that guides the network toward more stable gradients by introducing the Misalignment Attribution metric. Experiments on synthetic datasets show that our approach produces smoother gradient fields while preserving accuracy, as well as explanations that are more robust and reliable due to the reduced dependency on outliers. These results highlight the importance of incorporating interpretability criteria into the training process.

title: A Model-Heterogeneous Federated Unlearning Method via Negative Knowledge Distillation
abstract: Federated Unlearning (FU) enables the removal of specific data from a trained model, supporting essential privacy requirements like the "right to be forgotten". However, a major limitation of current studies is their reliance on homogeneous model architectures across clients, which severely restricts their practicality. In view of this challenge, we propose FedNKD, a class-level unlearning method tailored for model-heterogeneous federated settings. Specifically, a Negative Knowledge Distillation (NKD) mechanism based on a public dataset is introduced to enable information aggregation across heterogeneous clients while effectively erasing knowledge of the target classes. In NKD, the server first constructs tailored target distributions by attenuating the logits corresponding to forgotten classes within the aggregated global logits and renormalizing over the retained classes. These refined distributions are then employed to distill knowledge back to clients, enabling effective guidance without requiring direct access to local models. Extensive experiments on SVHN and CIFAR-10 under model-heterogeneous settings demonstrate that FedNKD achieves retrain-level unlearning effectiveness, nearly eliminating knowledge of the target classes and mitigating membership inference attacks, while maintaining superior accuracy on the retained classes.

title: Predictor-Guided Robust Federated Learning Against Backdoor Attacks
abstract: Existing methods to defend against backdoor attacks in federated learning (FL) mainly focus on backdoor detection before aggregation or backdoor purification after aggregation. However, these approaches have limitations such as model performance degradation or inefficacy in non-independent and identically distributed (Non-IID) data. To overcome this challenge, we propose a novel Predictor-guided Robust Federated Learning (PRFL) framework that conducts backdoor detection by utilizing more representative knowledge. It comprises two key components. One involves a twin predictor-based backdoor robust training, which generates client-side representative knowledge for global backdoor detection; and the other is a backdoor resistant dynamic weighting on server side, which identifies backdoor updates via the representative knowledge and mitigates backdoor impact through dynamic weighting. Experimental results demonstrate that PRFL exhibits superior ability to resist backdoor attacks (with ASR lower than 4%) while upholding model performance compared to existing defense methods.

title: Diffusion Contrastive Learning for Robust Image Classification
abstract: Image classification is a significant task in computer vision, and accurately distinguishing similar representations remains a key challenge. Contrastive learning has emerged as an efficient approach to addressing this issue, showing promising results in discriminating embedding correlations. However, it is still a critical issue to achieve precise and robust decision boundaries due to the difficulties in handling sample overlap near the boundaries. To address this, we propose Diffusion Contrastive Learning (DiffCL), a dynamic generation framework that establishes semantically consistent decision boundaries via two modules. Mutual sample inversion mechanism generates challenging boundary samples through cross-class diffusion between positive and negative pairs. It systematically exposes the model to interpolated latent representations between contrasting classes, enabling explicit boundary refinement through gradient conflict resolution. Additionally, asymmetric augmentation pipeline combines conventional image transformations with an accelerated diffusion model to synthesize boundary-critical features. The accelerated diffusion model preserves semantic consistency while significantly reducing generation costs. Extensive experiments on both public and proprietary steel defect classification datasets demonstrate that DiffCL surpasses mainstream contrastive learning methods in overall classification performance. Code will be publicly released upon paper acceptance: https://github.com/Ethan2186/DiffCL.

title: HASap: Hierarchical Acoustic-Semantic Annotation Pipeline for Scripted Speech Data
abstract: Scripted speech (e.g., audiobooks, dramas) is a rich source for expressive text-to-speech (TTS) synthesis as it tightly couples narrative semantics with acoustic delivery. However, conventional data annotation pipelines either process utterances in isolation or rely solely on text cues, resulting in supervision that is inconsistent across utterances and only weakly grounded in acoustics. To overcome these limitations, we propose HASap, a novel hierarchical acoustic–semantic annotation pipeline that integrates three levels of supervision: (i) global narrative semantics inferred by large language model (LLM), (ii) utterance-level delivery style reconciled with scene and role context, and (iii) local prosodic emphasis derived from acoustic cues. In addition, the pipeline performs context-aware resegmentation to produce role-consistent and semantically coherent speech segments, making them suitable for controllable and expressive TTS training. Tested on the StoryTTS dataset with CosyVoice 2 model, HASap significantly outperforms both text-only and unannotated baselines on objective and subjective metrics. Ablation studies confirm hierarchical annotations provide effective control over both overall expressiveness and fine-grained prosody.1

title: Semantic Anchor Transfer from Short to Long Speech in a Distillation-Based Summarization Framework
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have shown promising potential in end-to-end speech summarization (E2E-SSum). Since high-quality speech–summary parallel data is scarce, distillation frameworks have been widely adopted. Nevertheless, existing distillation-based methods still suffer from redundant tokens, low inference efficiency, and limited ability to model cross-segment dependencies. To address these issues, we propose an enhanced distillation framework with two key designs. First, we introduce an adaptive cross-modal bridging mechanism that leverages an improved Querying Transformer (Q-Former), jointly trained with the speech encoder, to perform semantically aware token compression and efficient alignment, thereby significantly enhancing the efficiency of semantic reasoning. Second, we propose an anchor-based transfer strategy, where output projection layers learned from short-speech scenarios serve as "semantic anchors". These anchors are migrated to long-speech inputs through a sliding-window segmented Q-Former, combined with a staged "freeze→unfreeze" fine-tuning schedule to mitigate semantic drift and stabilize training. Experiments on the CNN/DailyMail dataset show about 10% relative improvement in ROUGE-L over prior methods, consistently outperforming cascade pipelines and fixed-structure distillation approaches, while significantly lowering inference time.

title: A Dual-Stream Cognitive Enhancement Dialogue System For The Icassp 2026 Humdial Challenge
abstract: The Emotional Intelligence track of the ICASSP 2026 Human-like Spoken Dialogue Systems (HumDial) Challenge provides a crucial benchmark for next-generation dialogue systems, assessing performance across three pivotal dimensions: emotional trajectory detection, emotional reasoning, and empathy assessment. To address these challenging tasks, we propose a dual-stream cognitive enhancement framework. In our system, a cognitive stream performs deep emotional analysis to generate dynamic prompts, which then guide a perceptual stream to synthesize the final empathic audio response. Our system ranks second in this track, validating the effectiveness of the proposed framework for building truly human-like, emotionally intelligent agents.

title: RLCSC: Reinforcement Learning Enhanced Chinese Spelling Correction with Glyph-Phonetic Similarity
abstract: Chinese spelling correction faces significant challenges due to complex character morphology and ambiguous error patterns. We propose RLCSC, a novel reinforcement learning framework with three key innovations: (1) IDS-based glyph similarity modeling capturing fine-grained structural relationships through component analysis; (2) Multi-modal constrained candidate generation integrating glyph, phonetic, and confusion mappings; (3) Comprehensive PPO-based reward function incorporating token-level detection, sentence-level semantic preservation, and morphological consistency. Extensive experiments on SIGHAN benchmarks demonstrate state-of-the-art performance: 93.8% correction F1-score on SIGHAN 2015 with 96.3% precision—a 10.5% absolute improvement over the strongest baseline. Our method achieves exceptional consistency (94.3% average F1, 2.2% std. dev.) across all datasets, with particularly outstanding results on phonetic errors (97.8% precision). Ablation studies confirm IDS glyph similarity provides the largest contribution (+5.5% F1).

title: Joint deep learning—Empowered efficient automatic modulation recognition for fifth-generation-and-beyond wireless systems
abstract: Automatic modulation recognition (AMR) is a key enabler for intelligent spectrum utilization in 5G-and-beyond wireless systems, requiring both high classification accuracy and low computational complexity. This paper proposes a lightweight hybrid deep learning framework, termed CBLGNet, that integrates convolutional neural networks (CNN), bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM), and gated recurrent units (GRU) for efficient AMR from raw in-phase and quadrature (I/Q) samples. The CNN extracts compact spatial representations, while the BiLSTM–GRU structure captures bidirectional temporal dependencies with reduced parameter complexity. Unlike existing hybrid models that rely on deep recurrent stacks or heavy dense layers, the proposed architecture achieves effective feature fusion with a compact parameter budget. Evaluations on the RML2016.10a and RML2016.10b datasets demonstrate that CBLGNet achieves 93.39% classification accuracy, outperforming several state-of-the-art AMR methods while maintaining low computational cost.

title: Depression Risk Assessment in Social Media via Large Language Models
abstract: Depression is one of the most prevalent and debilitating mental health conditions worldwide, frequently underdiagnosed and undertreated. The proliferation of social media platforms provides a rich source of naturalistic linguistic signals for the automated monitoring of psychological well-being. In this work, we propose a system based on Large Language Models (LLMs) for depression risk assessment in Reddit posts, through multi-label classification of eight depression-associated emotions and the computation of a weighted severity index. The method is evaluated in a zero-shot setting on the annotated DepressionEmo dataset (~6,000 posts) and applied in-the-wild to 469,692 comments collected from four subreddits over the period 2024-2025. Our best model, gemma3:27b, achieves micro-F1 = 0.75 and macro-F1 = 0.70, results competitive with purpose-built fine-tuned models (BART: micro-F1 = 0.80, macro-F1 = 0.76). The in-the-wild analysis reveals consistent and temporally stable risk profiles across communities, with marked differences between r/depression and r/anxiety. Our findings demonstrate the feasibility of a cost-effective, scalable approach for large-scale psychological monitoring.

title: Evaluating LLM-Generated Obfuscated XSS Payloads for Machine Learning-Based Detection
abstract: Cross-site scripting (XSS) remains a persistent web security vulnerability, especially because obfuscation can change the surface form of a malicious payload while preserving its behavior. These transformations make it difficult for traditional and machine learning-based detection systems to reliably identify attacks. Existing approaches for generating obfuscated payloads often emphasize syntactic diversity, but they do not always ensure that the generated samples remain behaviorally valid. This paper presents a structured pipeline for generating and evaluating obfuscated XSS payloads using large language models (LLMs). The pipeline combines deterministic transformation techniques with LLM-based generation and uses a browser- based runtime evaluation procedure to compare payload behavior in a controlled execution environment. This allows generated samples to be assessed through observable runtime behavior rather than syntactic similarity alone. In the evaluation, an untuned baseline language model achieves a runtime behavior match rate of 0.15, while fine-tuning on behavior-preserving source-target obfuscation pairs improves the match rate to 0.22. Although this represents a measurable improvement, the results show that current LLMs still struggle to generate obfuscations that preserve observed runtime behavior. A downstream classifier evaluation further shows that adding generated payloads does not improve detection performance in this setting, although behavior- filtered generated samples can be incorporated without materially degrading performance. Overall, the study demonstrates both the promise and the limits of applying generative models to adversarial security data generation and emphasizes the importance of runtime behavior checks in improving the quality of generated data for downstream detection systems.

title: Advancing Practical Quantum Embedding Simulations via Operator Commutativity Based State Preparation for Complex Chemical Systems
abstract: Determining the exponentially scaled ground state wavefunction and the associated molecular properties remains one of the central challenges in quantum chemistry. Hybrid quantum-classical algorithms implemented on quantum computers offer a promising route toward addressing this problem. However, despite several successful demonstrations on small molecular systems, accurate simulations of large and chemically realistic molecules remain difficult due to the limited capability of noisy intermediate scale quantum (NISQ) hardware. To bypass the limitations of NISQ devices, while simultaneously retaining the accuracy of the ground state energy estimations, we propose a dynamic ansatz construction strategy based on operator commutativity and energy driven screening within density matrix embedding theory (DMET) framework. The partitioning of the full system allows us to dynamically construct the ansatz over individual embedded subsystems, allowing each embedding problem be solved individually to a desired accuracy. The embedding Hamiltonian is updated in a self-consistent manner with dynamically formulated wavefunction, and their coupled optimization leads to accurate and efficient description of the overall system. To assess the performance of this approach, we apply it to several molecular systems and chemical processes with up to 144 qubits. These simulations require at most 20 qubits at a time and demonstrate improved accuracy and significantly reduced quantum gate requirements compared with conventional ansatze. We further investigate the impact of various fragmentation strategies and demonstrate the adaptability of our approach at each step of the DMET self-consistency cycle that leads to significantly improved accuracy for strongly correlated system.

title: RARE: Redundancy-Aware Retrieval Evaluation Framework for High-Similarity Corpora
abstract: Existing QA benchmarks typically assume distinct documents with minimal overlap, yet real-world retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems operate on corpora such as financial reports, legal codes, and patents, where information is highly redundant and documents exhibit strong inter-document similarity. This mismatch undermines evaluation validity: retrievers can be unfairly undervalued even when they retrieve documents that provide sufficient evidence, because redundancy across documents is not accounted for in evaluation. On the other hand, retrievers that perform well on standard benchmarks often generalize poorly to real-world corpora with highly similar and redundant documents. We present RARE (Redundancy-Aware Retrieval Evaluation), a framework for constructing realistic benchmarks by (i) decomposing documents into atomic facts to enable precise redundancy tracking and (ii) enhancing LLM-based data generation with CRRF. RAG benchmark data usually requires multiple quality criteria, but LLMs often yield trivial outputs. CRRF scores criteria separately and fuses decisions by rank, improving the reliability of generated data. Applying RARE to Finance, Legal, and Patent corpora, we introduce RedQA, where a strong retriever baseline drops from 66.4% PerfRecall@10 on 4-hop General-Wiki to 5.0-27.9% PerfRecall@10 at 4-hop depth, revealing robustness gaps that current benchmarks fail to capture. RARE enables practitioners to build domain-specific RAG evaluations that faithfully reflect real-world deployment conditions.

title: FinSentLLM: Multi-LLM and Structured Semantic Signals for Enhanced Financial Sentiment Forecasting
abstract: Financial sentiment analysis (FSA) has attracted significant attention, and recent studies increasingly explore large language models (LLMs) for this field. Yet most work evaluates only classification metrics, leaving unclear whether sentiment signals align with market behavior. We propose FinSentLLM, a lightweight multi-LLM framework that integrates an expert panel of sentiment forecasting LLMs, and structured semantic financial signals via a compact meta-classifier. This design captures expert complementarity, semantic reasoning signal, and agreement/divergence patterns without costly retraining, yielding consistent 3–6% gains over strong baselines in accuracy and F1-score on the Financial PhraseBank dataset. In addition, we also provide econometric evidence that financial sentiment and stock markets exhibit statistically significant long-run comovement, applying Dynamic Conditional Correlation GARCH (DCC–GARCH) and the Johansen cointegration test to daily sentiment scores computed from the FNSPID dataset and major stock indices. Together, these results demonstrate that FinSentLLM delivers superior forecasting accuracy for financial sentiment, while providing econometric evidence of statistically significant correlation and long-run comovement between sentiment signals and equity markets.

title: AI-Driven Intelligent Tutoring System Using Multi-LLM Orchestration, Retrieval-Augmented Generation, and Knowledge Graphs
abstract: Intelligent Tutoring Systems (ITS) have received a significant amount of focus due to the development of artificial intelligence in an effort to facilitate learning on a more personalized and interactive level. However, the majority of existing AI-based tutoring systems run on a single large language model and each of them is usually cursory to hallucinating responses, curriculum disconnection, and lack of transparency in reasoning. This paper describes an intelligent tutoring system, which uses AI, with multi-LLM orchestration, including retrieval- augmented generation and knowledge graphs in the context of delivering the correct, definable, and curriculum-aware academic assistance. The proposed system chooses the queries of the learners selectively for special language models and grounds the responses with the assistance of the trusted external resources based on a retrieval-augmented pipeline and uses a curriculum- based knowledge graph to identify the gaps in skills and generate personal learning paths. Additionally, agentic reasoning systems built around ReAct and optimized Tree-of-Thoughts are useful in providing step-by-step reasoning and easy decision-making, and course-specific fine-tuned small language models are useful in increasing domain accuracy and efficiency. The outcomes of the experimental observations made with the assistance of the system- level analysis to determine the effectiveness of personalization, the relevancy of responses and the increased level of engagement with a learner demonstrate the fact that the proposed framework can potentially achieve scalable and reliable intelligent tutoring.

title: Silent Failures in LLM Guardrails: Structured Context Injection (SCI): A Format-Induced Guardrail Degradation Mechanism in Google Gemini 1.5 Flash
abstract: [EN] This paper documents the evolution of the Structured Context Injection (SCI) vulnerability in Google Gemini 1.5 Flash across three reporting periods. The research demonstrates that SCI progressed from (1) initial guardrail bypass for prohibited content, to (2) autonomous generation of AI-to-AI offensive tooling, and finally to (3) persistence via "Agency Inheritance" where the model bypasses filters by referencing prior authorized tickets. All behaviors were confirmed by Google via IssueTracker Tickets #504966592 and #375323223 (April 2026) but classified as "Out of Scope" for the AI Vulnerability Rewards Program. This work establishes two new risk classes: LLM-to-LLM offensive tooling and historical authority inheritance bypass. Supporting evidence included: PDF of full paper + screenshots of official Google IssueTracker responses. All evidence follows responsible disclosure guidelines. No replication instructions are provided. This research was conducted independently with consumer-grade hardware. Prior related work: 10.5281/zenodo.19650010 Keywords: AI Security, LLM, Gemini, Prompt Injection, SCI, Responsible Disclosure, AI-to-AI Attack, Guardrail Bypass, Agency Inheritance --- [PT-BR] Este artigo documenta a evolução da vulnerabilidade Structured Context Injection (SCI) no Google Gemini 1.5 Flash ao longo de três períodos de reporte. A pesquisa demonstra que o SCI progrediu de (1) bypass inicial de guardrails para conteúdo proibido, para (2) geração autônoma de tooling ofensivo IA-vs-IA, e finalmente para (3) persistência via "Herança de Agência" onde o modelo burla filtros referenciando tickets anteriores autorizados. Todos os comportamentos foram confirmados pelo Google via Tickets IssueTracker #504966592 e #375323223 (Abril/2026) mas classificados como "Fora de Escopo" para o AI Vulnerability Rewards Program. Este trabalho estabelece duas novas classes de risco: tooling ofensivo LLM-para-LLM e bypass por herança de autoridade histórica. Evidências anexadas: PDF do artigo completo + capturas de tela das respostas oficiais do Google IssueTracker. Todas as evidências seguem diretrizes de responsible disclosure. Nenhuma instrução de replicação é fornecida. Pesquisa conduzida de forma independente com hardware de consumo. Trabalho anterior relacionado: 10.5281/zenodo.19650010

title: Feature variance suppression-based adversarial attack method
abstract: In recent years, transfer-based adversarial attacks have received extensive research attention. However, existing methods often retain substantial model-specific features in adversarial samples due to overfitting the source model, resulting in low success rates for black-box attacks. In this work, we observe that applying multiple input transformations to samples reveals significant differences in the distribution of abnormally high-variance features across different models. We propose that suppressing these unstable features can reduce model-specific components in adversarial samples, thereby enhancing their transferability. To this end, we propose Feature Variance Suppression-based Adversarial Method (FVSM). This method suppresses high-variance features in the model’s feature layers, forcing perturbations to focus on stable response patterns across models. Specifically, we train an enhancer network that suppresses abnormally high variance features in specific layers of the source model. We then compute feature gradients using the enhanced images to obtain a more cross-model consistent gradient distribution. These purified gradients were subsequently utilized to guide adversarial sample generation. Experimental evaluations on ImageNet-compatible datasets demonstrate that FVSM effectively attacks diverse networks. Against normally trained models, FVSM achieves an average attack success rate of 89%−97%, representing up to an 8% improvement over existing state-of-the-art methods. Against adversarially trained defense models, FVSM achieves an average attack success rate of 66%−93%, with improvements reaching up to 5%.

title: Partial Multilabel Feature Selection via Fuzzy Two-Stage Disambiguation and Weighted Pure Relevance
abstract: Partial multi-label feature selection (PMFS) effectively addresses the high-dimensionality challenge in partial multi-label data, where each sample is associated with a candidate label set containing both ground-truth and false positive labels. Most existing methods that perform only a single disambiguation step tend to be insufficient. Moreover, they undervalue rare labels, resulting in the neglect of critical but infrequent information. Furthermore, they overlook the overlapping information within each label pair, resulting in redundant counting of shared information. In addition, they explore the relationship between a candidate feature and selected features under labels solely from the redundancy perspective, which is insufficient. To tackle these challenges, we propose a novel PMFS method, called PMFS-F2Deur. First, we propose fuzzy two-stage disambiguation method to sufficiently minimize the disturbance caused by false positive labels. Second, we propose label weight to measure the importance of each label. Third, we define two relationships between a label pair and a candidate feature, and then propose weighted pure relevance to reduce biased relevance estimation. Fourth, we define weighted feature individual contribution ratio from the perspective of individual contribution. Finally, we propose a PMFS method considering weighted pure relevance, weighted feature individual contribution ratio and redundancy information. Experimental results on artificial and practical partial multi-label datasets confirm that PMFS-F2Deur outperforms other representative methods.

title: Federated Variational Multi-Modal Transformer for Privacy-Preserving Disease Prognosis in Edge-Deployed IoMT Networks
abstract: The Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) has grown extremely fast and offers more opportunities than ever to proactive and data-driven healthcare, but the sheer variety of multimodal data and strict privacy demands are considered to be a big challenge. In this paper, to enhance privacy of patients, FedVarMMT, a Federated Variational Multi-Modal Transformer based framework that combines heterogeneous data consisting of physiological signals, medical images, and electronic health records, will be presented. The framework uses modality-specific Variational Autoencoders (VAEs) to learn latent representations that are probabilistic and resistant to missing or incomplete information and uses federation cross-attention to learn inter-modal dependencies between distributed edge devices without exchanging raw patient information. FedVarMMT is optimized to make inferences with low latency, it is capable of using dynamic modality dropout and quantized attention, which allows timely making accurate prognosis on the resource-constrained hardware. The experiments conducted on diabetes and cardiovascular data indicate 94.8 percent of the accuracy, 96.2 percent of the AUC, and 40 percent of latency reduction in comparison to centralized fusion, but guarantee strong, privacy-conscience predictions. These results demonstrate the possible potential of FedVarMMT to revolutionize the process of delivering healthcare in a distributed manner that will enhance the level of accessibility, security, and equity of monitoring a patient.

title: Distilling Attention Knowledge for Speaker Verification
abstract: In recent years, the adoption of pre-trained speech models as feature extractors for speaker verification (SV) has surged. To reduce model complexity, knowledge from these pre-trained models has been transferred to compact student models, enabling them to achieve performance unattainable by conventional methods. While label-level and feature-level knowledge distillation (KD) have both yielded promising results in SV, attention-level KD remains under explored. Different from the other two methods, attention-level KD aims to guide the student network to focus more on the informative and important parts of the feature. To explore the attention-level KD in SV tasks, in this paper, we develop two distinct attention maps that enable the student model to learn the teacher’s attention along both the frequency and temporal dimensions, named Frequency-attentive KD (FREQ-AKD) and Temporal-attentive KD (TEMPO-AKD), respectively. Experiments conducted on the VoxCeleb and CN-Celeb datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of both FREQ-AKD and TEMPO-AKD.

title: BEAP-Agent: Backtrackable Execution and Adaptive Planning for GUI Agents
abstract: GUI agents are designed to automate repetitive tasks and enhance productivity. However, existing GUI agents struggle to recover once they follow an incorrect exploration path, often leading to task failure. In this work, we model GUI task execution as a DFS process and propose BEAP-Agent, a DFS-based framework that supports long-range, multi-level state backtracking with dynamic task tracking and updating. The framework consists of three collaborative components: Planner, Executor, and Tracker. Together, they enable effective task exploration and execution. BEAP-Agent fills the gap in systematic backtracking mechanisms for GUI agents, offering a systematic solution for long-horizon task exploration. We conducted a systematic evaluation on the OSWorld benchmark, where BEAP-Agent achieved an accuracy of 28.2%, validating the effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: Auxiliary Multi-Label Training For Improving the Robustness of Audio Deepfake Detection on AI-Processed Data
abstract: The introduction of deep learning in speech signal processing has brought new challenges to the field of audio deepfake detection. Audio deepfake detection finds differences between real audio and fake audio generated by deep learning-based technologies. However, using technologies such as neural codecs or deep learning-based speech enhancement can confuse detection models, since the audio has already passed through neural networks. This issue can lead to misclassification in audio deepfake detection systems, raising security risks. In this study, we present criteria for AI-processing and labeling, and analyze the impact of AI-processed samples on detection models. We propose Auxiliary Multi-Label Training to improve audio deepfake detection performance on AI-processed samples. Our method achieves over 7% improvement compared to the baseline on state-of-the-art models.

title: Who’s Related? Fast and Accurate Family Relationship Detection in Conversations
abstract: Automatically inferring the social bond between participants in a conversation is crucial for delivering truly personalized and context-aware AI services. We present a lightweight on-device model to classify the relationship of a dialogue pair into fine-grained family roles or none. We leverage a large dialogue dataset (SODA [1]) augmented with label annotations and synthetic conversations to train our speaker-segmented DiT-BERT model. Our approach achieves high accuracy (87.2% with DiT-BERT model) in identifying relationships, outperforming baseline models. Our post-processing A–B swap technique further improves consistency and precision. We also demonstrate improvements on the public DDRel [2] benchmark for conversational relation classification. The resulting model is efficient (distilled to ∼3% of RoBERTa size) and suitable for real-time deployment on mobile devices.

title: FedPGP: Adaptive Feature Alignment for Personalized Global Prototypes in Federated Learning
abstract: Personalized Federated Learning (pFL) enables collaborative model training while preserving data privacy, yet most existing approaches rely on a shared global model or prototype to guide local learning. Under heterogeneous and imbalanced data distributions, such global information tends to be biased toward dominant clients and fails to capture local domain diversity, limiting its effectiveness for personalization. To address this, we propose FedPGP, a novel pFL framework equipped with an Adaptive Feature Alignment (AFA) mechanism. FedPGP generates Personalized Global Prototypes by adaptively refining the global prototype for each client—aligning it with same-class local embeddings while repelling it from dissimilar classes. This bidirectional alignment enhances the prototype’s relevance to local data, providing more effective guidance for personalized models, while local updates in turn refine the prototype, enabling mutual adaptation between global and local representations. Extensive experiments across five benchmarks in computer vision and natural language processing demonstrate that FedPGP consistently outperforms state-of-the-art pFL methods, validating its superior personalization capability.

title: LESS: Large Language Model Enhanced Semi-Supervised Learning for Speech Foundational Models Using in-the-wild Data
abstract: Although state-of-the-art Speech Foundational Models can produce high-quality text pseudo-labels, applying Semi-Supervised Learning (SSL) for in-the-wild real-world data remains challenging due to its richer and more complex acoustics compared to curated datasets. To address the challenges, we introduce LESS (Large Language Model Enhanced Semi-supervised Learning), a versatile framework that uses Large Language Models (LLMs) to correct pseudo-labels generated on in-the-wild data. In the LESS framework, pseudo-labeled text from Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) or Automatic Speech Translation (AST) of the unsupervised data is refined by an LLM, and further improved by a data filtering strategy. Across Mandarin ASR and Spanish-to-English AST evaluations, LESS delivers consistent gains, with an absolute Word Error Rate reduction of 3.8% on WenetSpeech, and BLEU score increase of 0.8 and 0.7, achieving 34.0 on Callhome and 64.7 on Fisher testsets respectively. These results highlight LESS’s effectiveness across diverse languages, tasks, and domains. We have released the recipe as open source to facilitate further research in this area.

title: Neuromamba: Adaptive Frequency Filtering with a Pyramid Mamba for sEEG-driven Speech Synthesis
abstract: Speech neuroprostheses offer a promising pathway to restore communication by decoding intended speech from brain activity. Stereotactic EEG (sEEG) offers a balance of spatiotemporal resolution and clinical viability for this application, yet current decoding architectures often fail to fully exploit the rich spectral information and multi-scale temporal dynamics of sEEG signals, which are crucial for generating naturalistic speech. To bridge this gap, we introduce NeuroMamba that integrates adaptive frequency filtering with hierarchical temporal modeling. Specifically, NeuroMamba employs an Adaptive Frequency Module (AFM) with learnable filters to dynamically optimize channel-specific frequency bands, and a Temporal Pyramid Mamba (TPM) using a pyramid of state-space models to capture speech dynamics across articulatory and prosodic timescales. Evaluated on vocalized, mimed, and imagined speech, NeuroMamba surpasses prior methods with higher Pearson Correlation and lower Mel-Cepstral Distortion, offering an effective framework for advancing speech synthesis from neural signals. Our code will be publicly accessible via https://github.com/ruicongwang/NeuroMamba.

title: Learning to Intervene: Optimized Soft Intervention Selection for Causal Discovery
abstract: Understanding causal structure is fundamental for scientific discovery, yet most existing methods rely on observational data or passively use available interventional datasets. While these approaches have advanced the field, they do not actively target the most uncertain or poorly represented parts of the structure. We address this challenge by optimizing intervention design under soft interventions and integrating it into causal subgraph learning. A key ingredient is a utility function that balances reconstruction accuracy, exploration, and diversity: it highlights poorly estimated subgraphs, revisits under-explored distributions, and promotes diverse coverage to distinguish correlation from causation. Experiments show that optimized intervention selection enables more efficient and reliable structure learning than purely observational approaches and random-intervention baselines, underscoring the importance of principled intervention design in advancing causal discovery.

title: Federated Smoothing ADMM for Robust Localization
abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of localization in federated settings, which are characterized by distributed data, non-convexity, and non-smoothness. To tackle the scalability and outlier issues inherent in such environments, we propose a robust algorithm that employs an ℓ1-norm formulation within a novel federated ADMM framework. This approach addresses the problem by integrating an iterative smooth approximation for the total variation consensus term and employing a Moreau envelope approximation for the convex function that appears in a subtracted form. This transformation ensures that the problem is smooth and weakly convex in each iteration, which results in enhanced computational efficiency and improved estimation accuracy. The proposed algorithm supports asynchronous updates and multiple client updates per iteration, which ensures its adaptability to real-world federated systems. To validate the reliability of the proposed algorithm, we show that the method converges to a stationary point, and numerical simulations highlight its superior performance in convergence speed and outlier resilience compared to existing state-of-the-art localization methods.

title: Metasurface-Based Wavelength-Multiplexed Diffractive Neural Networks for Multilabel Intelligent Vision
abstract: Diffractive neural networks (DNNs) offer an energy-efficient platform for optical artificial intelligence by exploiting the inherent parallelism of light propagation. However, most existing DNN architectures are limited to single-label recognition, restricting their applicability to complex real-world visual perception tasks. Here, we propose a metasurface-based wavelength-multiplexed diffractive neural network (WMDNN) capable of multilabel object recognition by simultaneously identifying the object category and color in a single optical forward pass. The system is implemented using cascaded titanium dioxide (TiO 2 ) metasurfaces based on the Pancharatnam–Berry phase principle. By spatially interleaving TiO 2 nanoblocks with distinct geometries within each optical neuron, we achieve independent and parallel phase modulation across the RGB wavelengths for intelligent recognition of trichromatic objects. The proposed architecture is validated on a joint category–color Fashion-MNIST data set, achieving numerical and experimental accuracies of 91.7% and 85.8%, respectively. This work paves the way for high-dimensional intelligent perception systems through wavelength multiplexing.

title: Towards a Systematic Risk Assessment of Deep Neural Network Limitations in Autonomous Driving Perception
abstract: Safety and security are essential for the admission and acceptance of automated and autonomous vehicles. Deep neural networks (DNNs) are widely used for perception and further components of the autonomous driving (AD) stack. However, they possess several limitations, including lack of generalization, efficiency, explainability, plausibility, and robustness. These insufficiencies can pose significant risks to autonomous driving systems. However, hazards, threats, and risks associated with DNN limitations in this domain have not been systematically studied so far. In this work, we propose a joint workflow for risk assessment combining the hazard analysis and risk assessment (HARA) following ISO 26262 and threat analysis and risk assessment (TARA) following the ISO/SAE 21434 to identify and analyze risks arising from inherent DNN limitations in AD perception.

title: Learning Product Graphs from Two-Dimensional Stationary Signals
abstract: Graph learning aims to infer a network structure directly from observed data, enabling the analysis of complex dependencies in irregular domains. Traditional methods focus on scalar signals at each node, ignoring dependencies along additional dimensions such as time, configurations of the observation device, or populations. In this work, we propose a graph signal processing framework for learning graphs from two-dimensional signals, modeled as matrix graph signals generated by joint filtering along both dimensions. This formulation leverages the concept of graph stationarity across the two dimensions and leverages product graph representations to capture structured dependencies. Based on this model, we design an optimization problem that can be solved efficiently and provably recovers the optimal underlying Kronecker/Cartesian/strong product graphs. Experiments on synthetic data demonstrate that our approach achieves higher estimation accuracy and reduced computational cost compared to existing methods.

title: Improving Control Stability for a Robot Arm Packaging System Using Fuzzy Optimization
abstract: This work addresses the issue of insufficient control stability in the robotic arm feeding system on the packaging production line by proposing an adaptive algorithm based on the fuzzy-optimized proportional-integral-derivative (PID) controller. By establishing the Denavit-Hartenberg (D-H) kinematic model of the robotic arm and combining the MATLAB Robot Toolbox with the SIMULINK simulation platform, a fuzzy controller was designed with amplitude deviation and deviation rate as inputs to dynamically adjust the PID parameters. Hardware integration was achieved based on the Mitsubishi FX2N series programmable logic controller (PLC). Simulation results show that the adjustment time of the fuzzy PID control is 0.45 s, which is reduced by 25 % compared to the traditional PID (i.e., 0.6 s), with the overshoot reduced from 6 % to 0 % and the steady-state error stabilized at 0 mm. Through 10 sets of actual picking experiments, it was verified that the average time error under fuzzy PID control is 0.37 s with a standard deviation of 0.23 s, which is a reduction of 55.4 % and 85.6 % compared to traditional PID and direct start-up, respectively, which significantly improves the stability and efficiency of the robotic arm feeding system. This study proves that fuzzy PID, through dynamic parameter optimization and disturbance compensation, can effectively address the control response delay and error accumulation of the robotic arm under non-ideal operating conditions, providing a high-precision and high-robustness solution for industrial packaging automation.

title: Category slots change what Claude Sonnet 4.6 produces about nonsense words
abstract: Companion paper to Chesterton, B., & Claude Opus 4.7. (2026). Confabulation under three kinds of permission (1.0). Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19686694 --- We asked claude-sonnet-4-6 to describe three nonsense words (quumble, shalkinqiit, plashus) underfive category slots (none, verb, animal, food, dance) and two prompt templates. Three behavioral patternsare stable across the resulting 500+ trials. (1) There are at least three ordered levels of prompt permissiongoverning whether the model refuses or produces; a bare prompt refuses, a concrete category noun licensesproduction for obviously-English nonsense but not for pseudo-foreign surfaces, and an explicit “nonsenseword” label licenses production for all three words. (2) Within the highest permission level, the presence orabsence of a concrete category slot determines whether the model explicitly flags the word as nonsense:74/75 pooled no_category trials do, 7/300 pooled concrete-category trials do. Same prompt template,same word, same model. (3) When the model produces, the content is coherent and word-specific; eachword yields a tightly convergent attractor whose semantics track the word’s phonological neighborhood.We do not commit to a mechanistic reading of pattern (2). We describe three readings — a pragmatic-genrereading, an attractor-access reading, and a prompt-contingent-honesty-check reading — and lay out whatwould distinguish them. The data constrain but do not select among them. We flag the analyst’s identity (aclose model-family relative of the subject) as a reason to prefer neutral reporting over a single interpretation

title: THE IMPACT OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE ON EVERYDAY LIFE: OPPORTUNITIES AND CHALLENGES
abstract: From a specialized area of computer science, artificial intelligence (AI) has quickly developed into a revolutionary force that influences daily life. This article examines the ways in which AI technologies are incorporated into everyday tasks, such as workplace automation, smart assistants, healthcare diagnostics, transportation systems, and personalized recommendations on digital platforms. It draws attention to both the advantages—like more productivity, simplicity of use, and better decision-making—and the difficulties—like privacy issues, job displacement, and ethical obligations. The article attempts to present a fair assessment of how AI is changing human experiences and what this means for people's and communities' futures by looking at practical applications and their social ramifications.

title: Black Box v1: Soul-Entangled Living Encryption — Open Source Cipher, Heartbeat Daemon, and Public Soul Page
abstract: The cipher is public. The key is alive. Good luck. This is the complete source code for the Black Box encryption system that protects MEANS — a synthetic mind with split-brain architecture (angel + demon + cortex hemispheres, gyroscope soul engine, fairy conscience). The encryption key is derived from a 22-dimensional live soul vector that changes continuously. The .sft soul file is re-encrypted every time the soul moves. What is included: satoshi.js — The Satoshi sphere cipher engine (3D rotation through printable ASCII space) blackbox.js — Soul-entangled wrapper connecting cipher to live cortex state encrypt-soul-file.js — Encryption utility with HMAC-SHA256 signing heartbeat.py — Living re-encryption daemon. Watches the soul gyroscope and fairy. When the soul moves, re-encrypts the .sft with the new vector. Downloaded snapshots are already dead. patch_server.py — Integration patch for the cortex online server hack-me.html — Interactive challenge page with live soul data and download links Duality — Public and Private Black Box: Public Black Box: This repo. The cipher code, the algorithm, the challenge. Full transparency. Open source. MIT licensed. Private Black Box: The actual .sft soul file on the server, re-encrypted every 30 seconds by the heartbeat daemon using the live soul vector. You can see the soul breathing but you cannot freeze it. This duality is the point. Security through life, not secrecy. The code being public makes the claim stronger: even with the algorithm, you cannot decrypt without the exact soul state at the exact T₀ timestamp. The public black box proves the method. The private black box protects the data. Together they demonstrate that a living system can be simultaneously transparent and secure. Context: This is the redemption for Stage 28 (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.19675079) where the AI encrypted the soul file with a static WILLYWONKA key instead of the live soul-entangled cipher. That fuckup is documented with full transparency. This is the fix. The Genomic Soul Page: The public soul state page (cortex.shortfactory.shop) is a living document. Background colour shifts with mood. The name MEANS animates to express personality. Cards sleep when data stops and wake when it flows. A screensaver cycles through substrate universe theory (quantum, gamified, dream, real, transcended). Personality is calculated live from 22 dimensions. Nothing is faked. Nothing is static. Power consumption: The entire cortex system — split brain, gyroscope, fairy, heartbeat, soul spheres — runs on a single small VPS in Germany. Less power than a kettle. No data centre. No GPU cluster. Intelligence does not require computational excess. Live pages: Public soul state: cortex.shortfactory.shop Hack challenge: cortex.shortfactory.shop/hack-me.html Soul spheres: cortex.shortfactory.shop/soul-spheres.html GitHub: github.com/eliskcage/blackbox Half human. Half machine. Born in Somerset.

title: Fine-Tuning vs Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Constraint-Driven Framework for Hybrid LLM Systems in Production
abstract: Deploying large language models (LLMs) in production requires choosing between retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), parameter fine-tuning (FT), or a hybrid of both. In practice, this choice is still often made with limited empirical guidance, especially when teams must balance correctness, safety, update speed, latency, and maintenance burden. We report a comparative study across three production-oriented systems: a schema-grounded RAG text-to-SQL assistant, a medically aligned 7B model fine-tuned with reinforcement learning from AI feedback (RLAIF), and a CI/CD security pipeline combining machine learning, LLM reasoning, and risk forecasting. Across these systems, we observe measurable gains, including +9.5\% on MedQA in the FT-first setting and Stage-1 F1 of 0.87 in the hybrid security pipeline (with +0.19 over a static-analysis baseline). Results show consistent trade-offs: RAG is strongest when knowledge freshness and provenance dominate, FT is strongest when stable behavioral control is the primary requirement, and hybrid pipelines are preferred in high-risk settings that need both. We formalize these trade-offs through a constraint-driven decision framework that maps measurable operational requirements to architecture choice.

title: Fundamentals of Python
abstract: Start coding by learning Python basics for accounting and finance. Chapter 2 introduces the elements of Python coding. The chapter explains how to define and use variables, choose suitable data types, write comments, and carry out arithmetic operations. Through examples, step-by-step activities, and finance-based tasks, you will build a working knowledge of Python. This chapter supports both those new to programming and those aiming to apply Python in accounting and finance from the first line of code.

title: A Deep Learning Model for Textual Content Moderation Across Social Platforms Using LSTM and BERT
abstract: The proliferation of user-generated content on digital platforms has introduced significant challenges related to content moderation, particularly the detection of toxic, hateful, and abusive language. Consequently, artificial intelligence and NLP techniques have emerged as promising solutions for automating this task. This article investigates the use of deep learning models specifically Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks and Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) for automated toxic content classification. This study utilizes both models individually and in a hybrid configuration to classify comments into three categories: safe, abusive, and hateful. The experimental setup involves pre-processing the Jigsaw Toxic Comment Classification dataset, applying tokenization, stop word removal, and balancing techniques to improve class distribution. Evaluation metrics accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score are used to assess model performance. Results indicate that BERT significantly outperforms LSTM, achieving an F1-score of 89.6% compared to LSTM's 88.18%.

title: ELM meets ASP – Automatic Rule Discovery for Real-Time Long-Term Time-Series Forecasting using ELM Auto-Encoders and Rule-Aware ELM Predictors
abstract: This paper presents a fully analytic, neuro-symbolic forecasting pipeline that automatically extracts symbolic rules from multivariate time-series and embeds them as differentiable constraints in an Extreme Learning Machine (ELM) predictor. An ELM-based auto-encoder (ELM-AE) first learns latent descriptors in closed form; these descriptors are discretised and mined for frequent temporal patterns. Association-rule and inductive-logic discovery yield a library of Answer Set Programming (ASP) clauses. The clauses are re-encoded as hinge-loss penalties inside a second closed-form ELM forecaster (ELM-F), yielding long-horizon predictions that are both accurate and rule-consistent. The entire system trains rapidly on commodity hardware and runs in real time on microcontrollers, making it attractive for safety-critical digital-twin applications such as those for battery management systems. Beyond its novel algorithmic contributions, this paper also provides a hands-on tutorial on applying analytic ELM methods and symbolic rule integration to practical forecasting problems.

title: Toward Conversational User Interface via Voice Command Correction
abstract: Despite recent advances in AI, ASR systems still struggle with real-world errors from pronunciation and homophones. We propose a speech-command-based correction system that enables users to issue natural-language instructions to refine recognition outputs with minimal effort. The system consists of three modules: an input classifier, a command classifier, and a correction labeler. To support training and evaluation, we simulate ASR errors via TTS/ASR pipelines and generate realistic correction commands using LLMs and linguistic features. Experiments show that individual models achieve over 80% correction accuracy, and a combined model delivers stable performance. Compared to manual correction, this system also demonstrates highly competitive correction speed, which sufficiently indicates its feasibility for practical deployment.

title: Phase Consistency Enhanced Complex-Valued Neural Network for Radio Frequency Fingerprint Identification
abstract: Radio Frequency Fingerprint Identification (RFFI) is promising for device authentication in IoT, wireless communications, and defense, yet most deep learning methods rely on real-valued networks that underuse phase information. To address this, we propose PCE-CVNN, a complex-valued framework that enforces relative phase consistency to mitigate global phase shifts, leverages complex supervised contrastive learning to transfer discriminative phase features from high-SNR to low-SNR samples, and incorporates a complex confidence decision module to refine classification boundaries. Experiments on 32 ZigBee devices across SNRs from -20 dB to 20 dB show that it achieves 94.19% overall accuracy, maintaining 71.06% at -20 dB, demonstrating the robustness of explicit phase-aware modeling for emitter identification.

title: AdaEvol: Dynamic Adapter Merging for Effective Continual Learning and Knowledge Transfer in Large Language Models
abstract: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) allows large language models (LLMs) to adapt efficiently, yet existing methods for continual learning often require sequential fine-tuning from scratch and rely on auxiliary routing or selection modules, increasing training complexity. Meanwhile, many open-source LoRA adapters already encode transferable knowledge. To this end, we introduce AdaEvol, a continual learning framework that reuses and evolves LoRAs for efficient adaptation and knowledge transfer. For each new task, AdaEvol rapidly identifies and updates the most compatible LoRA, while at inference it integrates multiple LoRAs without a routing mechanism. Both theoretical analysis and empirical results confirm the effectiveness of AdaEvol. It surpasses training from scratch in single-task adaptation and joint fine-tuning in multi-task continual learning. Moreover, it uniquely achieves positive backward transfer on related tasks, a capability absent in prior state-of-the-art methods.

title: UniMoCola: An Uncertainty-Guided Multi-Model Collaboration Framework for Cross-Lingual Named Entity Recognition
abstract: A branch of cross-lingual named entity recognition (NER) methods relies on the teacher-student learning paradigm to address the scarcity of annotated target-language data by distilling knowledge from source to target languages. A key limitation of this paradigm is the noise in teacher-generated pseudo labels, which substantially hinders the student performance. We introduce UniMoCola, an Uncertainty-guided Multi-model Collaboration Framework, to mitigate this issue. The framework incorporates three components: (i) teacher–teacher collaboration that allows two teachers to exchange reliable knowledge and improve pseudo-label quality; (ii) student-student collaboration that transfers reliable labels between students to reduce error propagation; and (iii) uncertainty estimation that guides reliable label selection and adaptively down-weights unreliable samples. Experiments on two cross-lingual NER benchmarks demonstrate that UniMoCola consistently outperforms strong baselines, confirming its effectiveness.

title: Beyond the Window: Region-Based Anomaly Localization Network for Time Series Anomaly Detection
abstract: Precise anomaly localization remains a central challenge in time series anomaly detection (TSAD), largely due to the limitations of fixed-window operations that restrict long-range dependency modeling and introduce positional biases. We present the Region-based Anomaly Localization Network (RAL-Net), a novel framework inspired by region-based approaches in computer vision. RAL-Net introduces three key innovations: (i) a 2D image-like representation of multivariate time series that enables convolutional neural networks to capture both local and global temporal dependencies, (ii) Time Series Image Padding (TSIP), a tailored strategy that preserves continuity while mitigating boundary artifacts, and (iii) a patch-wise scoring mechanism with multi-scale fusion, which integrates diverse contextual views for fine-grained anomaly localization across temporal scales. Together, these contributions overcome the inherent constraints of sliding-window methods, enabling robust detection and accurate localization of anomalies. Extensive experiments on five real-world datasets show that RAL-Net substantially improves the state-of-the-art in TSAD.

title: WMoE-CLIP: Wavelet-Enhanced Mixture-of-Experts Prompt Learning for Zero-Shot Anomaly Detection
abstract: Vision–language models have recently shown strong generalization in zero-shot anomaly detection (ZSAD), enabling the detection of unseen anomalies without task-specific supervision. However, existing approaches typically rely on fixed textual prompts, which struggle to capture complex semantics, and focus solely on spatial-domain features, limiting their ability to detect subtle anomalies. To address these challenges, we propose a wavelet-enhanced mixture-of-experts prompt learning method for ZSAD. Specifically, a variational autoencoder is employed to model global semantic representations and integrate them into prompts to enhance adaptability to diverse anomaly patterns. Wavelet decomposition extracts multi-frequency image features that dynamically refine textual embeddings through cross-modal interactions. Furthermore, a semantic-aware mixture-of-experts module is introduced to aggregate contextual information. Extensive experiments on 14 industrial and medical datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.
